legal.p.intro: This policy explains what OpenMeru Mail collects when you use a mailbox at openmeru.com, why, and what you can do about it.
legal.p.store1: Account data: your name, your @openmeru.com address, a hashed password, an optional recovery email, signature, profile photo and forwarding address.
legal.p.store2: Your mail: messages you send and receive, with their attachments, kept so you can read them in your mailbox.
legal.p.store3: Technical data: session cookies that keep you signed in, the date of your last sign-in, your language choice and, if you turn them on, the browser push subscription used for new-mail notifications.
legal.p.use: Only to run your mailbox: deliver and show your mail, send what you write, notify you of new messages, let you recover access and keep the service secure. We do not sell your data and we do not use your messages for advertising.
legal.p.who1: Our server provider hosts the application and the database.
legal.p.who2: Cloudflare receives incoming mail for openmeru.com and passes it to your mailbox.
legal.p.who3: Brevo relays the mail you send.
legal.p.who4: Your browser's push service (for example Google, Apple or Mozilla) delivers notifications if you enable them.
legal.p.private: A mailbox only shows its own messages. Administrators can manage accounts and may open a mailbox when that is needed to provide support or keep the service secure.
legal.p.keep: Your mail stays until you delete it. Messages in Trash can be deleted for good at any time. When an account is deleted, its messages, attachments and profile photo are removed.
legal.p.choice1: Edit your profile, change your password or set forwarding in Settings.
legal.p.choice2: Turn notifications on or off on each device.
legal.p.choice3: Delete your account and all its mail from Settings → Delete account.
legal.t.intro: These terms apply to every mailbox at openmeru.com provided by OpenMeru Mail. By signing in you accept them.
legal.t.account1: Keep your password private. You are responsible for what is sent from your mailbox.
legal.t.account2: Tell us at hello@openmeru.com if you think someone else has access to it.
legal.t.useLead: You must not use OpenMeru Mail to:
legal.t.use1: send spam, bulk unsolicited mail or phishing;
legal.t.use2: send malware or try to break into other systems or accounts;
legal.t.use3: harass, threaten or impersonate other people;
legal.t.use4: break the law or the rights of others.
legal.t.useEnd: We may limit, suspend or close a mailbox that breaks these rules.
legal.t.service: We work to keep OpenMeru Mail available and your mail safe, but the service is provided as it is. Delivery to other providers can be delayed or filtered by them. Keep your own copies of anything important.
legal.t.end: You can delete your account at any time in Settings → Delete account. This removes the mailbox and all its mail and cannot be undone.
legal.t.changes: We may update these terms. The date at the top shows the latest version.

landing.title: OpenMeru: open-source email for your own domain
landing.metaDescription: OpenMeru Mail is an open-source webmail you run on your own server. Send with Brevo, receive with Cloudflare Email Routing, and keep a copy of everything in Gmail.
landing.ogDescription: Self-hosted webmail with an admin panel, 10 languages, two-factor authentication and push notifications. No mail server to run.
landing.lead: OpenMeru Mail is a self-hosted webmail. You get an admin panel, mailboxes, a rich editor, two-factor authentication, push notifications and 10 languages. Send through Brevo or any SMTP relay, receive with Cloudflare, and keep a copy of everything in Gmail.
landing.f1: Create, search, open and delete you@yourdomain.com mailboxes at /admin. Admins sign in with a password plus a code sent by email.
landing.f2: Each mailbox sees only its own mail. Inbox, sent, drafts, starred, archive, spam and trash.
landing.f3: Formatting, Cc/Bcc, attachments up to 25 MB, signatures, replies and auto-forwarding.
landing.f4: Google Authenticator, Authy or any TOTP app, with recovery codes. The admin can make it mandatory for every account.
landing.f5: English, Português (BR and PT), Español, Français, Deutsch, Italiano, Nederlands, Русский, 中文.
landing.f6: No Postfix, no IMAP, no port 25. Just PHP, MySQL and two free services. Your name, logo and colours on every screen.
landing.demoLead: Look around before you install. The demo is read-only: nothing is sent, received or saved, so click anything you like.
landing.demoMailboxText: Sign in as :email. Try the inbox, search, the editor, settings, themes and the 10 languages.
landing.demoAdminText: See the admin panel with sample mailboxes: create, search, edit and open accounts, plus the sending settings.
landing.howText: Brevo delivers what you send. Cloudflare accepts what you receive and passes it to a small Worker. The Worker always sends a copy to your Gmail, then delivers the message to your server. If your server is down, nothing is lost.
landing.needServerText: A Linux VPS with PHP 8.5, MySQL 8 or MariaDB, Composer and nginx or Apache. CloudPanel makes it easy.
landing.needDomainText: Its DNS must be on Cloudflare. The free plan is enough.
landing.needBrevoText: Sends your mail. The free plan includes 300 emails per day. brevo.com (or any other SMTP relay).
landing.needGmailText: Receives a copy of every incoming message (the catch-all) and the admin sign-in codes. Create one just for the project.
landing.s1t: Create a Gmail for the catch-all
landing.s1p: Create a new Gmail account, for example yourproject@gmail.com. It does two jobs:
landing.s1a: It's the Cloudflare destination address, which gets a copy of every message sent to any address on your domain.
landing.s1b: It's the ADMIN_OTP_EMAIL, which gets the 6-digit code each time someone signs in to /admin.
landing.s2t: Install the app on your server
landing.s2p1: Create a MySQL database first (CloudPanel: Databases → Add Database) and keep its name, user and password at hand. Then sign in to your server over SSH as the site user (in CloudPanel, the user of the site you created for your domain) and run one line:
landing.s2p2: It checks PHP and Composer, downloads the app into ~/openmeru-app, installs the dependencies and asks you, one by one, for your domain, the Gmail for the sign-in codes, the database and the first admin. Passwords are typed, never shown or stored in your shell history. It generates the keys, creates the tables and prints the two values you will need in Cloudflare.
landing.s2p3: Prefer to see every step? The same thing by hand:
landing.s2p4: Point your web server at the public_root folder: set the site's document root to ~/openmeru-app/public_root (CloudPanel: Settings → Root Directory → yourdomain.com/openmeru-app/public_root when the app lives inside the site folder). Updates are then just the same one line again.
landing.s2note: Turn on HTTPS. Let's Encrypt in CloudPanel and the Cloudflare proxy both work. When you're done, https://yourdomain.com/ shows the sign-in page. Run php artisan openmeru:install again at any time: it keeps what is set and only asks for what is missing. Do step 3 before opening /admin: the sign-in code travels by email.
landing.s3a: Create an account at brevo.com.
landing.s3b: Go to Senders, Domains & Dedicated IPs → Domains → Add a domain and enter yourdomain.com.
landing.s3c: Brevo shows DNS records: a Brevo code, DKIM and DMARC. Add each one in Cloudflare → DNS → Records, with the proxy off (grey cloud) on CNAMEs. Then click Verify in Brevo.
landing.s3d: Add a sender on your domain: hello@yourdomain.com. The system sender must be on your domain, or the relay drops the sign-in codes.
landing.s3e: Go to SMTP & API → SMTP → Generate a new SMTP key. Copy the login (xxxx@smtp-brevo.com) and the key.
landing.s3f: Save them in /admin → Settings → Sending (pick Brevo, SMTP2GO, Mailgun, Postmark, SendGrid, Amazon SES, Resend or any SMTP server), or from the terminal; the - asks for the key without showing it:
landing.s3note:
One SPF record only. Cloudflare and Brevo both need SPF, so merge them into one TXT record:
v=spf1 include:_spf.mx.cloudflare.net include:spf.brevo.com ~all
landing.s4a1: Open your domain in Cloudflare, then go to Email → Email Routing → Enable. Let it add its MX records.
landing.s4a2: Go to Destination addresses → Add and enter your Gmail. Confirm the verification email in Gmail.
landing.s4b1: Go to Workers & Pages → Create → Worker, name it openmeru-mail-inbound, then click Deploy.
landing.s4b2: Click Edit code and paste the contents of cloudflare-email-worker.js. Then click Deploy.
landing.s4b3: Go to Settings → Variables and Secrets and add:
landing.s4c: c. Route mail to the Worker.
landing.s4c1: Catch-all → Worker (simplest): Email Routing → Routing rules → Catch-all address → Edit, action Send to a Worker, pick openmeru-mail-inbound, turn it on. Every address on the domain reaches OpenMeru and new mailboxes work at once.
landing.s4c2: One rule per mailbox (safest when the domain already forwards mail elsewhere): leave the catch-all as it is and add a rule name@yourdomain.com → Send to a Worker → openmeru-mail-inbound for each mailbox you create.
landing.s4note: Either way every message goes to Gmail too. Addresses with no mailbox stay in Gmail only.
landing.s5a: Open https://yourdomain.com/admin and sign in. The code arrives in your Gmail.
landing.s5b: Create a mailbox, for example test@yourdomain.com.
landing.s5c: Sign in at https://yourdomain.com/ and send a message to your Gmail.
landing.s5d: Reply from Gmail. The reply shows up in the inbox within seconds.
landing.s5note: If mail doesn't arrive, check Workers → openmeru-mail-inbound → Logs (a 403 means the secrets don't match), the Email Routing Activity log, and storage/logs/laravel.log.
landing.updatingText: Every install checks openmeru.com once a day. When a newer version is out, /admin shows Update now: database backup, new code, dependencies, migrations and caches, with the log on screen. Or run the install line again on the server:
landing.q1: Do I need to open port 25 or run Postfix?
landing.a1: No. Brevo sends and Cloudflare receives. Your server only serves HTTPS.
landing.q2: Can I use IMAP or Outlook?
landing.a2: Not yet. OpenMeru is a webmail. For a desktop client, use auto-forwarding to another inbox, or the Gmail copy.
landing.a3: The software is MIT-licensed. Brevo's free plan sends 300 emails per day, and Cloudflare Email Routing and Workers are free for normal use.
landing.q4: Where are my passwords and keys stored?
landing.a4: Mailbox passwords are hashed. Two-factor secrets, the SMTP and API keys are encrypted with your APP_KEY. Nothing secret goes in git, so back up your .env.
landing.q5: Can I use another SMTP provider?
landing.a5: Yes. Settings → Sending has presets for Brevo, SMTP2GO, Mailgun, Postmark, SendGrid, Amazon SES and Resend, and any other SMTP relay that lets you send as your domain works.
landing.q6: Can people create their own mailbox?
landing.a6: Yes, when the admin turns it on in Settings → Security. A sign-up page then lets anyone register an address on your domain.
